steps.title: Your first day at Contoso
say: It's Alex's first day at Contoso, and the company hands over a Microsoft 365 account.
So what actually arrives with it?
Not just Word and PowerPoint — a whole platform. Apps, email, storage, collaboration, identity and security, all in one subscription.
Before Copilot can help with any of this work, it's worth knowing what the work sits on.

steps.title: Subscription, licence, account
say: Nothing unlocks until three things line up.
Contoso buys a subscription — a plan. A seat from that plan is assigned to Alex as a licence. And a user account is created: alex at contoso dot com.
Miss the middle one, and the apps stay locked. The account exists, but the services won't open.
Subscription, licence, account — that's the order, and the licence is what turns a locked app into a working one.

steps.title: Signing in to the company tenant
say: Alex signs in with the work email, and lands somewhere specific.
That account belongs to Contoso's tenant — the company's own isolated space inside Microsoft 365.
The tenant holds the users and identity, Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and the policies that govern them.
It's a boundary. Everything Alex does from here happens inside it.

steps.title: A day of work — and the data it creates
say: Now Alex actually works. Answer a customer in Outlook, join the standup in Teams.
Draft the proposal in Word, build the deck in PowerPoint, update the forecast in Excel.
Ordinary things — a mail, a chat, a slide. But every one of them leaves something behind.
All of it becomes company work data, sitting in the tenant.

steps.title: Where does everything go?
say: So where does a day's work actually land?
Mail and calendar in Outlook. Chats and meetings in Teams. Alex's own files in OneDrive, and the shared team files in SharePoint.
Different services, one pile — emails, meetings, chats, documents, decks and files.
All of it stays inside Contoso's tenant. Remember that map, because it's exactly what Copilot will read later.

steps.title: How the company protects it
say: Company data is valuable, so administrators don't leave it open.
A sensitivity label classifies a file — Public, Internal or Confidential. Alex's Q four Proposal dot docx gets Confidential.
Then Alex tries to share it outside, with partner at outside dot com, and the policy engine checks the request first.
Public is allowed, Internal gets a warning, Confidential is blocked. Labels classify; policies decide.

steps.title: Desktop apps or just a browser
say: The same account works two ways, and Alex doesn't have to choose once and for all.
There are the installed desktop apps on the laptop — and there's microsoft three sixty five dot com, in any browser, with nothing to install.
Alex opens Word for the web, edits, and it saves straight back to OneDrive.
Same file, same account, same tenant. Only the door is different.

steps.title: Now meet Microsoft 365 Copilot
say: After a few weeks, the tenant holds a lot: emails, meetings, chats, documents and decks.
Microsoft 365 Copilot lets Alex simply ask about that work. Summarise last week's emails and prepare a meeting brief — and back comes the answer, with Outlook, Teams and SharePoint listed as sources.
Without it: search, read, analyse, write. With it: ask, review, use.
Microsoft 365 creates the work. Microsoft 365 Copilot helps you work with it — and that's exactly where the journey goes next.

Antes de que Copilot pueda ayudar con este trabajo, conviene saber sobre qué se apoya ese trabajo.

Suscripción, licencia, cuenta: ese es el orden, y la licencia es lo que convierte una aplicación bloqueada en una que funciona.

El inquilino guarda los usuarios y la identidad, Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint y las directivas que los gobiernan.
Es una frontera. Todo lo que Alex haga a partir de aquí ocurre dentro de ella.

Redacta la propuesta en Word, monta la presentación en PowerPoint y actualiza la previsión en Excel.
Cosas corrientes: un correo, un chat, una diapositiva. Pero cada una deja algo detrás.
Todo eso se convierte en datos de trabajo de la empresa, alojados en el inquilino.

say: ¿Y dónde acaba realmente un día de trabajo?
El correo y el calendario en Outlook. Los chats y las reuniones en Teams. Los archivos propios de Alex en OneDrive, y los archivos compartidos del equipo en SharePoint.
Servicios distintos, un mismo conjunto: correos, reuniones, chats, documentos, presentaciones y archivos.

steps.title: How the company protects it
say: Los datos de la empresa valen mucho, así que los administradores no los dejan al aire.
Una etiqueta de confidencialidad clasifica el archivo: público, interno o confidencial. La propuesta del cuarto trimestre, Q cuatro Proposal punto docx, recibe la etiqueta confidencial.
Entonces Alex intenta compartirla fuera, con partner arroba outside punto com, y el motor de directivas revisa la petición antes de nada.
Lo público se permite, lo interno recibe un aviso, lo confidencial se bloquea. Las etiquetas clasifican; las directivas deciden.

Están las aplicaciones de escritorio instaladas en el portátil, y está microsoft tres sesenta y cinco punto com, en cualquier navegador, sin instalar nada.

steps.title: Your first day at Contoso

say: さあ、Alex の実務が始まります。Outlook でお客様に返信し、Teams で朝会に参加する。 Word で提案書を書き、PowerPoint で資料を組み立て、Excel で見通しを更新する。 どれもふつうの作業です。メール一通、チャット一言、スライド一枚。でも、そのたびに何かが残ります。 そのすべてが、テナントの中に置かれる会社の業務データになります。

say: では、一日分の仕事は実際どこへ行くのでしょう。 メールと予定表は Outlook。チャットと会議は Teams。Alex 自身のファイルは OneDrive、チームで共有するファイルは SharePoint です。 サービスは別々でも、中身はひとかたまり。メール、会議、チャット、ドキュメント、資料、ファイル。 そのすべてが Contoso のテナントの中にとどまります。この地図を覚えておいてください。あとで Copilot が読むのは、まさにここです。

say: 会社のデータには価値があります。だから管理者は、それを無防備にしておきません。 秘密度ラベルがファイルを分類します。公開、社内、社外秘。Alex の Q 四 Proposal ドット docx には、社外秘が付きます。 そこで Alex が社外の partner アット outside ドット com に共有しようとすると、ポリシーエンジンがまず要求を確認します。 公開なら許可、社内なら警告、社外秘ならブロック。ラベルが分類し、ポリシーが判断します。

steps.title: Desktop apps or just a browser
say: 同じアカウントで、入り口は二つ。Alex はどちらかに縛られるわけではありません。 ノート PC にインストールしたデスクトップアプリ。そして microsoft 三六五 ドット com なら、どのブラウザーからでも、インストールなしで使えます。 Alex が Word for the web を開いて編集すると、そのまま OneDrive に保存されます。 同じファイル、同じアカウント、同じテナント。違うのは入り口だけです。

구독, 라이선스, 계정. 이 순서이고, 잠긴 앱을 쓸 수 있는 앱으로 바꿔 주는 건 라이선스입니다.

steps.title: Signing in to the company tenant
say: Alex가 회사 메일로 로그인하면 도착하는 곳은 분명합니다.

테넌트에는 사용자와 ID, Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, 그리고 이들을 통제하는 정책이 함께 들어 있습니다.

steps.title: A day of work — and the data it creates
say: 이제 Alex가 본격적으로 일합니다. Outlook으로 고객에게 답장하고, Teams로 스탠드업에 들어갑니다.
Word로 제안서를 쓰고, PowerPoint로 자료를 만들고, Excel로 전망치를 갱신합니다.
다 평범한 일입니다. 메일 한 통, 채팅 한 줄, 슬라이드 한 장. 그런데 그때마다 무언가가 남습니다.
그 모두가 테넌트 안에 쌓이는 회사의 업무 데이터가 됩니다.

공개는 허용, 내부용은 경고, 기밀은 차단. 레이블이 분류하고, 정책이 결정합니다.

같은 파일, 같은 계정, 같은 테넌트. 다른 건 들어간 문뿐입니다.

Copilot이 없으면 검색하고, 읽고, 분석하고, 씁니다. 있으면 묻고, 확인하고, 씁니다.

E-mail e calendário no Outlook. Conversas e reuniões no Teams. Os arquivos do próprio Alex no OneDrive, e os arquivos compartilhados do time no SharePoint.
Serviços diferentes, um conjunto só: e-mails, reuniões, conversas, documentos, apresentações e arquivos.
